inputs.sbc_source: 10-K fiscal 2025 (FYE 2026-01-31) cash-flow add-back, XBRL ShareBasedCompensation $37.426M. Ulta tags no separate tax-withholding-on-net-settlement line and publishes no adjusted-EBITDA combined figure; withholding is small (RSU/PBRSU vesting on ~0.3M shares/yr) and is not added -- owner FCF is marginally overstated by it.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Saturday nearest 31 January (52/53 week). Metrics.csv labels by calendar year of FYE: FY2026 = Ulta 'fiscal 2025' (ended 2026-01-31); CSV 'Q2 2027'/'Q3 2027' are fiscal 2026 Q1/Q2 (XBRL label drift).
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 42.757M basic on the Q2 FY2026 10-Q cover (2026-08-24) + 0.107M dilutive securities (Q2 diluted 43.062M less basic 42.955M weighted). Held FLAT: SBC fully expensed in the flows; buybacks (~$0.9-1.8B/yr) are value-neutral here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), beta ~1.05, ERP 5.0% -> CoE ~9.6%; funded debt is only a seasonal revolver, so WACC ~ CoE less a token debt weight = 9.0%. Same WACC across scenarios (risk charged once via the scenario drivers).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: straight-line lease cost (~$400M/yr; Q2 FY26 $102.9M) sits inside SG&A/COGS, so GAAP EBITDA is already after rent. Treatment: rent in the flows; the ~$2.1B operating lease liability is NOT in net debt; lease_cost_pct_path 0. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing: US operating company / specialty retailer; no prior valuation or memory entry). FY0 = fiscal 2025 (FYE 2026-01-31): revenue $12,392.8M, operating income $1,533.0M, D&A $300.8M, GAAP EBITDA $1,833.8M (14.8%); adj EBITDA ex-SBC $1,871.2M (15.10%). Owner FCF = OCF 1,502.8 - capex 434.8 - SBC 37.4 = $1,030.5M; component cross-check (EBIT 1,533 x (1-24.9%) + D&A 301 - capex 435) = $1,017M ties within 1.5%. Interest income not stripped: the company is net debt at the latest balance sheet and net interest was -$1.8M in fiscal 2025. NET DEBT is the 2026-08-01 Q2 balance sheet (revolver $339.6M less cash $158.5M and ST investments $55.0M) -- a SEASONAL TROUGH: inventory builds for holiday and the revolver also funded buybacks; at FYE 2026-01-31 the same items were ~$432M net cash. Using the latest filing per house rule costs ~$13/share versus the year-end position. Fiscal 2025 included the $387M Space NK (UK luxury beauty) acquisition, outside FCF; fiscal 2026 growth is part inorganic until the July anniversary. GUIDANCE (8-K 2026-08-27, raised): fiscal 2026 net sales +6.7% to +7.2%, comps +3.2% to +3.7%, operating income +8.3% to +9.3%, diluted EPS $28.70-$29.00, capex $400-450M, buyback plan raised to $1.8B. H1 fiscal 2026 revenue $6,199.5M (+10.0% y/y incl. Space NK).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 12.7% vs EPS 2.1% (and owner FCF -2.9%): book value is not a usable growth anchor for Ulta -- it is shaped by ~$0.9-1.5B/yr of buybacks against ~$1.0B owner FCF, so equity moves with the pace of repurchases, not with earnings power. All 5yr CAGRs start from fiscal 2020 (FYE Jan-2021), the COVID store-closure trough, and are inflated (EPS 52.5%, revenue 15.0%).
historical_growth.notes: Labels follow Metrics.csv (calendar year of FYE). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF less SBC (no interest-income strip; Ulta has held little net cash and earned trivial interest). SBC is ~0.3-0.5% of revenue, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are almost identical -- SBC is not funding the growth. Owner FCF has gone sideways ($1.13B fiscal 2022 -> $1.03B fiscal 2025) as operating margin fell from ~15.5% to ~12.4% while revenue grew ~6.7%/yr; EPS growth (2.1%/yr) is almost entirely buyback-driven. Selected growth 6.7% (3yr revenue) is the near-term anchor, decelerated toward terminal in the base.

base.wc_capture_note: Retailer: inventory (~19% of sales) less payables and gift-card/loyalty deferred revenue nets to ~5% of sales, so growth consumes ~5c per $ of incremental revenue.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY26 15.35% = guided operating income (+8.8% midpoint, ~$1,668M) + D&A ~$325M + SBC ~$40M on guided sales ~$13.26B. Held ~15.6%: below the fiscal 2019 (16.2% GAAP EBITDA) and fiscal 2022 (18.4%) levels, which were pre-competition and post-COVID boom respectively.

scenario_narratives.base: Ulta delivers the raised fiscal 2026 guide (sales ~+7%, operating income ~+9%), then settles into mid-single-digit growth: ~3% comps from loyalty (45M+ Ulta Beauty Rewards members), new-brand launches and wellness, 1-2% from ~50 net new US stores a year plus Space NK's UK/US rollout, fading to 3% by year 10 as the US store base saturates. 'Ulta Beauty Unleashed' cost work holds adj EBITDA ~15.5% -- recovering a little of the 2022-25 compression from shrink, wage and marketing investment, but not back to the post-COVID peak while Sephora-at-Kohl's and Amazon Premium Beauty keep promotions elevated. Capex trends to ~2.9-3.0% of sales as remodels dominate new builds.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prestige/mass beauty stays the most resilient consumer category and Ulta keeps taking share: Sephora's Kohl's partnership underdelivers as Kohl's shrinks, Target shop-in-shops and the Ulta marketplace/UB Media retail-media business scale, and Space NK becomes a credible second growth engine (UK plus US expansion, Middle East franchise). Growth runs 6-7% for five years and operating leverage, retail-media margin and lower shrink take adj EBITDA to ~17% -- between today and the fiscal 2022 high. Terminal growth 3%, 16x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Beauty normalises after a multi-year boom and Ulta's moat thins: Sephora (Kohl's ~850 shops plus own stores), Amazon Premium Beauty, TikTok Shop dupes and mass-channel prestige launches pressure traffic and force promotional loyalty spend. Fiscal 2026 lands at the low end of guidance (H1 already banked), then comps go flat-to-negative and growth is store-count only (~2%). Deleverage on a high fixed-cost lease base takes adj EBITDA from 15.1% to 13.0%; Space NK proves a low-margin distraction. Terminal growth 2%, 12x cap (a mature, share-donating retailer).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from the 15% default): owner FCF has gone sideways for three years while margins compressed, and the competitive axis (Sephora/Kohl's, Amazon) is structural, not cyclical. Base 50%: the raised fiscal 2026 guide with H1 banked makes year one low-risk. Bull 30% (down from 35%): it needs both share gains and a ~1.5pp margin recovery that the company has not guided to; balance-sheet risk is nil, so there is no case for a heavier bear tail.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ulta is a mature, cash-generative specialty retailer with negligible SBC (0.3% of revenue), so the house (SBC-expensed) and street bases sit close together; the valuation turns on margin durability against Sephora/Amazon competition and on how long mid-single-digit growth lasts. Buybacks shrink the count ~4-5%/yr but are value-neutral in this model -- they return the same owner FCF the DCF already counts.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin: each 1pp of adj EBITDA margin is worth roughly $40/share; the base holds ~15.6% vs 14.8% GAAP EBITDA in fiscal 2025.
Competition: Sephora at Kohl's, Amazon Premium Beauty and mass-channel prestige compress traffic and promotional economics.
Seasonal balance sheet: net debt is taken at the Q2 trough (2026-08-01); at fiscal year-end Ulta is typically ~$400M net cash (~$10-13/share).
Terminal value carries ~55-60% of EV; the 15x base cap binds (Gordon at 9%/2.5% is ~15.8x).
Space NK integration and international expansion are unproven at scale.
